This page maps the ideas on the other methods pages to the analysis code, as it stands now, and notes what is planned to change.

Think of the workflow in three steps: prepare the observations, fit the model, then turn the fit into a table or plot. An R object can hold any of these, so its name alone does not tell you whether it contains data, a fitted model or formatted output.

## Fitting and tables

[`fit_mixed_model()`](functions.qmd#fit-mixed-model) fits `outcome ~ time_factor * studyarm + (1 | study_id_screening)`, or the three-way version with a subgroup. [5. Fit mixed models](05_fit_mixed_models.qmd) fits each of the 56 analyses once: 5 outcomes overall, 5 outcomes × 4 subgroups, and 3 outcomes by child or adult, each in the intention-to-treat and per-protocol populations. Each fitted model then goes to the table, the estimates and, through the estimates, the plot.

[`tabulate_model_terms()`](functions.qmd#tabulate-model-terms) shows the raw coefficients described on [Longitudinal data and mixed models](methods_longitudinal.qmd) and [Interactions](methods_interactions.qmd): the baseline arm difference, the change-from-baseline differences at each visit, and the interaction terms. It doesn't show the arm effect in each subgroup level directly.

## Estimates and plots

[`estimate_effects()`](functions.qmd#estimate-effects) takes everything the plot shows from that one fitted model, with emmeans [@lenth2026emmeans]:

| Estimate | What it's used for |
|---|---|
| Mean in each visit × arm cell (and subgroup level), with its 95% confidence interval | The points and bars on the plot |
| Arm difference at baseline, and the visit × arm interaction at each follow-up (marked †), within each subgroup level | The p-values printed above each visit, or in each level's panel |
| Difference in that effect between each subgroup level and the first level | The row of p-values under each level after the first |

Degrees of freedom are Satterthwaite's, the same method as the model table, and p-values are not adjusted for multiplicity. An earlier version of the code refitted the same model in up to three other codings to read these numbers off as coefficients; emmeans gives the same numbers from the one fit (checked on synthetic data, [#10](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COHERO-RCT-analysis/issues/10)). Using one fit also means the means, the p-values and the table come from the same analysis rows.

[`compose_trajectory_figure()`](functions.qmd#the-whole-figure) draws those estimates, optionally over the individual trajectories. It fits nothing. By default it shows the means and the p-values for the contrasts; with `show_effect_panel = TRUE` it also shows each contrast's estimate and 95% confidence interval. At follow-up, the dagger-marked p-values concern change from baseline, not just the gap between the plotted means.

To read a plot, first identify the outcome, population, visit and subgroup. Then distinguish the individual observations, the fitted mean and its interval, and the particular contrast tested by each p-value. A visually separated pair of mean intervals is not a substitute for the corresponding contrast calculation.

## Count models

[4. Fit count models](04_fit_count_models.qmd) fits negative binomial models with log follow-up time as the offset, overall and with each arm × subgroup interaction, and reports exponentiated coefficients: IRRs, and for the interaction terms, ratios of IRRs. As with the mixed-model tables, the IRR in the non-reference level of a subgroup isn't shown directly. The separate alternative rescue fits retain an offset-syntax defect documented on the [count-model page](04_fit_count_models.qmd#rescue-models-alternative).

## What is planned to change

These are implementation proposals, not prerequisites for understanding the current analysis. Changing formatting and extracting a contrast can leave a model unchanged; changing the sample or formula can change the scientific comparison.

- [#8](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COHERO-RCT-analysis/issues/8): move all tables to gtsummary. The decision to report both kinds of table, the model terms and the effects within each subgroup level, is recorded there.
- [#25](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COHERO-RCT-analysis/issues/25): run the examples on these Methods pages on synthetic data, where the true effects are known.
